title: New York Man Sentenced to Five Years in Prison for Participating in a Nationwide Bank Fraud Conspiracy

evidence.passage: Attorney's Office,               Southern District of Alabama MOBILE, AL – A New York man was sentenced to 60 months in prison for participating in a nationwide bank fraud conspiracy involving stolen and counterfeited financial instruments.
Williams-Beverly admitted to agents that he produced counterfeited checks and coordinated the purchase and sale of stolen checks through the fraudulent Telegram channel he operated with Jackson.

Schimel, First Assistant United States Attorney for the Eastern District of Wisconsin, announced a settlement with Miracle-Ear, Inc., and the Miracle-Ear Foundation to settle claims that they improperly obtained three loans through the Paycheck Protection Program (“PPP”).

Miracle-Ear is wholly owned by Amplifon (USA) Inc., which, in turn, is wholly owned by Amplifon S.p.A., an Italian public company with thousands of employees and annual sales exceeding 1.5 billion euros in 2020 and 2021.
Miracle-Ear Foundation is likewise affiliated with Amplifon S.p.A.

Specifically, the United States alleges that Miracle-Ear and its foundation were not eligible for their PPP loans because they were affiliated with Amplifon S.p.A. and that the Amplifon corporate group employed too many individuals for Miracle-Ear and its foundation to qualify for PPP loans.
